# ducktel

> One binary that stores OpenTelemetry on disk and answers agent queries. OTLP/HTTP in, Parquet files out, DuckDB over those files.

You query it with MCP or with the CLI. The server does not interpret attribute keys for you.

Every MCP query tool requires `tenant`, and so do `list_services`, `list_metric_names`, and `list_attribute_keys`. The server keeps only rows whose `tenant.id` resource attribute equals that value. You cannot widen a query by omitting `tenant`. `list_tenants` takes no arguments and returns only tenant ids.

Time windows on `span_search`, `compare_spans`, `log_search`, `slow_requests`, and `metric_query` default to the last 60 minutes (`since_minutes`). `until_minutes` ends the window that many minutes before now. The default is 0, which means now. `until_minutes` must be less than `since_minutes`. `log_search` with `trace_id` and no `since_minutes` searches the whole history. `list_attribute_keys` also defaults to the last 60 minutes and samples at most 2000 rows per signal. It does not take `until_minutes`. A missing key is not proof the key never existed. `trace_lookup`, `flush_buffer`, `list_tenants`, `list_services`, and `list_metric_names` have no time window.

Saved MCP queries are per tenant. `save_query` validates the tool and arguments before writing. `run_saved_query` can override `since_minutes` and `until_minutes` for that run only.

Rows still in the receiver's memory buffer are not in the Parquet files yet. They are invisible to every query until a flush. The default flush interval is 30 seconds. If the MCP server was started with `--flush-url`, call `flush_buffer` and repeat the query.

## MCP tools

Registered by `Register` in `internal/mcp/server.go`. Thirteen tools are always registered. `flush_buffer` is registered only when a flush URL is set.

- [list_tenants](skills/ducktel/SKILL.md): tenant ids with stored telemetry. No arguments. Returns only tenant ids.
- [list_services](skills/ducktel/SKILL.md): service names for one tenant. Requires `tenant`. `source` omitted or `traces` reads spans. `source=logs` reads log records.
- [list_metric_names](skills/ducktel/SKILL.md): metric names for one tenant. Requires `tenant`.
- [list_attribute_keys](skills/ducktel/SKILL.md): attribute keys seen for one tenant. Requires `tenant`. Each row is `signal` (`traces`, `logs`, or `metrics`), `source` (`attributes` or `resource_attributes`), and `key`. Optional `signal`, `service_name`, `since_minutes` (default 60), and `limit` (default 200 per signal and source, cap 1000). Omitting `signal` still returns keys from each view, and `resource_attributes` are not dropped when `attributes` fills the cap. This is a sample of at most 2000 rows per signal, not every key ever stored.
- [trace_lookup](skills/ducktel/SKILL.md): one trace. Requires `trace_id` and `tenant`. `detail=summary` (the default) returns a compact summary. `detail=spans` returns every span and can be large. Attributes are included unless `include_attributes` is false. `limit` applies to `detail=spans` (default 1000).
- [span_search](skills/ducktel/SKILL.md): spans in a time window. Optional `service_name`, `filters`, `min_ms`, `max_ms`, and `limit` (default 100, cap 1000). Attributes are omitted unless `include_attributes` is true. A filter is `{key, value, op}`. `op` is `=` (default) or `!=`.
- [compare_spans](skills/ducktel/SKILL.md): why the slow spans differ from the rest of the same scope. The slow group defaults to spans slower than that scope's p95. Set `min_ms` and `max_ms` to choose the group yourself. Optional `service_name`, `span_name`, `span_kind`, and `filters`. `span_kind` defaults to `server` when `span_name` is omitted. `limit` defaults to 15 and caps at 50.
- [log_search](skills/ducktel/SKILL.md): log records, newest first. Optional `trace_id`, `service_name`, `severity`, `search` (body substring), `filters`, and `limit` (default 100, cap 1000).
- [slow_requests](skills/ducktel/SKILL.md): the slowest requests, each with a short trace summary. Pass `metric_name` to follow that metric's exemplars. Omit it to use the slowest root spans. `limit` defaults to 5 and caps at 20.
- [metric_query](skills/ducktel/SKILL.md): one metric over a window. Requires `metric_name` and `aggregation`. Aggregations are `avg`, `sum`, `min`, `max`, `count`, `p50`, `p95`, `p99`, `buckets`, and `exemplars`. Histograms are aggregated from their observations. A histogram result is not 0 just because the type is histogram. `buckets`, `p50`, `p95`, and `p99` need an explicit-bucket histogram. An exponential histogram supports `count`, `sum`, `avg`, `min`, and `max`. `group_by` takes a column (`service.name` means `service_name`), `attr.<key>`, or `resource.<key>`. `step` (`30s`, `1m`, `5m`, `1h`, or a number of seconds) adds a `time` column. At most 1500 buckets. `exemplars` ignores `step`. On a gauge or a sum, `count` counts exported points, not events.
- [list_saved_queries](skills/ducktel/SKILL.md): saved MCP queries for one tenant. Requires `tenant`. Returns `name`, `description`, `tool`, and `arguments`, sorted by name.
- [save_query](skills/ducktel/SKILL.md): save a read tool invocation for one tenant. Requires `tenant`, `name`, `tool`, and `arguments`. Optional `description`. Validates like a direct tool call before writing. Same name replaces the record.
- [run_saved_query](skills/ducktel/SKILL.md): run a saved query by name for one tenant. Optional `since_minutes` and `until_minutes` override the window for this run only.
- [flush_buffer](skills/ducktel/SKILL.md): asks the receiver to write its buffer. No arguments. Absent from the tool list when no flush URL is configured.

Row results are compact JSON, with no extra whitespace.

Span filters on `status_code` accept `ok`, `error`, or `unset`, and on `span_kind` accept `server`, `client`, `internal`, `producer`, or `consumer`, as well as the stored `STATUS_CODE_*` and `SPAN_KIND_*` values. `log_search` `severity=warning` also matches `WARN`, `err` matches `ERROR`, and `information` matches `INFO`. A bare dotted `group_by` such as `host.name` is rejected with a suggestion such as `resource.host.name`.

An empty result keeps its JSON as the first content block and adds a second text block that says how to recover: the tenant filter, the default window, the receiver buffer, an unrecognized `status_code` or `span_kind` spelling, and the discovery tools. An ungrouped `metric_query` whose value is null (no points matched, often a misspelled `metric_name`) gets the same block. `count` returns 0 without one.

Call `list_tenants` when you do not know the tenant. Call `list_services`, `list_metric_names`, or `list_attribute_keys` before you guess a service, a metric name, or a filter key.

For "why is this slow", call `slow_requests` first. Call `compare_spans` when you want the attribute values that show up more often on the slow spans. Call `metric_query` for a rate, a percentile, or a histogram. Follow a `trace_id` with `trace_lookup`, then `log_search`.

stdio, no token:

```bash
ducktel mcp --data-dir /data
```

HTTP. The read token is required. It is not the OTLP ingest token.

```bash
ducktel mcp --http --host 0.0.0.0 --port 4319 --data-dir /data \
  --auth-token "$DUCKTEL_MCP_TOKEN" \
  --flush-url http://localhost:4318/flush
```

Add `--dashboard` to serve the read-only UI at `/dashboard` and the JSON routes under `/api`. Those routes call the same query core as the tools. `DUCKTEL_AUTH_TOKEN` is the ingest (write) token. `DUCKTEL_MCP_TOKEN` is the query (read) token. Use different values.

## CLI

Global flags: `--data-dir` (default `./data`) and `--format json|table|csv` (default `json`).

- `ducktel query "<sql>"` runs DuckDB SQL on the `traces`, `logs`, and `metrics` views. It is not sandboxed. It will run DDL.
- `ducktel traces`, `ducktel logs`, and `ducktel metrics` are filtered shortcuts. `--since 0` means no time filter. `traces --limit` defaults to 20. `logs` and `metrics` default to 50.
- `ducktel schema [traces|logs|metrics]` prints columns.
- `ducktel services` lists service names seen in traces.
- `ducktel saved` stores and runs SQL you want to repeat. Nothing runs it on a schedule. MCP saved queries are a separate, tenant-scoped store: `list_saved_queries`, `save_query`, and `run_saved_query`.
- `ducktel testdata` sends synthetic OTLP to a receiver.
- `ducktel serve` is the receiver, not a query command. Default listen address is `localhost:4318`.

Column types and the histogram storage columns are in [skills/ducktel/references/schema.md](skills/ducktel/references/schema.md). SQL examples are in [skills/ducktel/references/queries.md](skills/ducktel/references/queries.md).
